items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: When he first came out I remember I was working with Tony Spargo... But when he first came out I didn't think very much of his music at all, in fact we hated it.

ctx.x: Correct. Certainly. Those poor fools haven’t got a clue I’m sorry to say. I mean if you want to teach jazz you take it back to where it’s able to be taught from and when it’s the most understandable, when it was still part of the popular culture, where the kids, that was their music. They were the rebels. Their parents looked at that kind of music, oh that’s awful, dreadful, jazz music. Even Miles Davis’ parents, you know, didn’t condone jazz music because it was the devil’s music, it was this kind of music, it…

Well I mean I look back, I look at him now and I almost shed a tear. When he first came out I remember I was working with Tony Spargo who was the original drummer with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, right? And he says, “Oh y’all are just jeal—” he had a southern, New Orleans accent, he said, “y’all are just jealous of him because he’s got such a pretty face.” But when he first came out I didn’t think very much of his music at all, in fact we hated it. It was gyrations and obscene, and there we are, very staid…
